steps.title: Prepare 0.8% agarose gel
steps.instruction: Combine 8.0 g agarose with 10 mM 1 M MOPS pH 7.6 and ddH₂O to a final volume of 1 L (≈0.8 % w/v). Autoclave, aliquot 15 mL portions into sterile centrifuge tubes, seal tightly and store at room temperature (stable ≤3 months).

steps.title: Prepare 1 M MOPS buffer pH 7.6
steps.instruction: Dissolve 209.27 g MOPS powder in 600–800 mL ddH₂O, adjust pH to 7.6 with KOH (use 10 N stock, add slowly near target pH). Bring volume to 1 L with ddH₂O, filter‑sterilize, wrap bottle in foil, store at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare 0.8 M MgSO₄ solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 96.3 g MgSO₄·7H₂O in ddH₂O and bring volume to 1 L. Autoclave immediately after preparation.

steps.title: Prepare CYE growth medium
steps.instruction: In 1 L total volume mix: 10 g BD Casitone (1 % w/v), 5 g BD yeast extract (0.5 % w/v), 10 mL 1 M MOPS pH 7.6 (10 mM), 10 mL 0.8 M MgSO₄ (8 mM), and 390 mL ddH₂O. Autoclave immediately after mixing.

steps.title: Grow bacterial culture to OD₆₀₀≈1
steps.instruction: Inoculate 25 mL CYE liquid medium in a 125 mL flask with the BN312 strain (or appropriate strain), add required antibiotics (e.g., moenomycin 4 µg/mL), and incubate at 32 °C with shaking until OD₆₀₀ ≈ 1. For other organisms adjust volume, medium and temperature (e.g., E. coli 2–5 mL LB at 37 °C).

steps.title: Make agarose pad on microscope slide
steps.instruction: Microwave‑melt the 0.8 % agarose gel, pipette 0.6 mL onto a clean microscope slide, gently place a second slide on top to spread, wait 2–3 min for solidification, then separate slides leaving a ~1 mm thick pad on one slide. If desired, add nutrients or inhibitors (e.g., moenomycin to 4 µg/mL) to the molten agarose before solidifying.

steps.title: Apply cell suspension to agarose pad
steps.instruction: Dispense 5 µL of the liquid cell culture onto the solidified agarose pad and let it air‑dry for 3–5 min.

steps.title: Cover pad with coverslip
steps.instruction: Gently place a VMR #1½ cover glass over the agarose pad, keeping it as close as possible to avoid bubble formation; avoid sudden movements.

steps.title: Set up microscope and focus sample
steps.instruction: Insert the prepared slide into the microscope, bring the sample into focus, and launch NIS‑Elements AR 5.30.02 (or equivalent software for other microscope brands).

steps.title: Configure ND acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Open ND Acquisition: under ‘Time’, set Interval to “no delay” and Loops to 100; under ‘Lambda’, select the 561‑nm laser in Opt. Conf. to enable automatic activation during imaging.

steps.title: Set fluorescence channel exposure and laser
steps.instruction: Switch to the fluorescence channel, select the 561‑nm laser, adjust its intensity as needed, and set the camera exposure time to 100 ms (giving 10 Hz imaging frequency and 100 ms temporal resolution).

steps.title: Select imaging field with ≥10 cells
steps.instruction: In DIC mode, locate a field containing at least ten well‑separated cells suitable for MATLAB analysis.

steps.title: Acquire brightfield reference image
steps.instruction: Capture a brightfield (DIC) image of the selected field; this image will be used later for cell identification.

steps.title: Activate PAmCherry with 405 nm laser
steps.instruction: Switch to the fluorescence channel, activate PAmCherry using the 405‑nm laser, limiting exposure to 2–3 s to minimize photobleaching. Adjust power as needed for the specific fluorophore.

steps.title: Record fluorescence time‑lapse at 10 Hz
steps.instruction: Immediately after activation, switch back to the 561‑nm laser and start acquisition using the predefined ND settings (Run Now). Record at 10 Hz (100 ms exposure) and, if needed, adjust TIRF angle, laser intensity, and camera gain to achieve ~1–2 activated particles per cell.

steps.title: Save image stack as TIFF
steps.instruction: When acquisition finishes, save the entire time‑lapse stack as a single .tiff file.

steps.title: Repeat imaging for hundreds of cells
steps.instruction: Move to a new field and repeat steps 9–15 until a few hundred individual cells have been imaged (minimum ≈ 100 cells from three biological replicates). Prefer fields with many isolated cells to reduce the number of repeats.

steps.title: Load MATLAB analysis script
steps.instruction: Start MATLAB and open the script “PALM2Dtracking_analysisauto2.m”.

steps.title: Set frame range and pixel size
steps.instruction: Edit lines 4–5: set first_frame = 1 and last_frame = 100. In line 8, after pixel_size=, enter the camera‑objective pixel size in µm.

steps.title: Enter exposure time and trajectory thresholds
steps.instruction: In line 9, after exposure_time=, input the exposure time in seconds (e.g., 0.1 s for 10 fps). In lines 10 and 12, set trajectory_length_low = 4 and trajectory_length_high = 12.

steps.title: Specify data folder keywords
steps.instruction: In line 17, after key_word=, type a unique part of the image directory name (e.g., ‘2026’, ‘DacB’, or ‘PAmCherry’) surrounded by single quotes. In line 18, after folder_name=, paste the full directory name (also in single quotes).

steps.title: Run cell selection and segmentation
steps.instruction: Click Run. In the cell‑selection window, draw a rectangle around each cell (click first vertex, drag to opposite vertex, click again, repeat for four vertices, double‑click to confirm). After all cells are selected, a second window shows brightfield on the left and the segmentation mask on the right; click the white mask region for each cell, press Enter, and discard poorly segmented cells.

steps.title: Execute analysis and wait for completion
steps.instruction: After confirming all cell outlines, the program runs automatically; processing may take several hours depending on data size and computer speed.

steps.title: Retrieve diffusion results files
steps.instruction: When analysis finishes, a result window appears and files are saved in the data folder: “bf_hist.tifff” (population MSD plot and diffusion coefficient bar graph), “bf_diffusion_coefficient.txt” (mean diffusion coefficient, error, particle count), and “bf_d_individual.txt” (individual cell coefficients).
